headline: Nvidia officially brings DLSS 5 to older RTX 40-series GPUs, but no full gamer control
summary: Nvidia confirms DLSS 5 will expand beyond RTX 50 to RTX 40-series GPUs later this fall. However, granular controls will remain exclusive to developers, not gamers.
details: Nvidia is officially expanding its DLSS 5 AI rendering technology beyond the upcoming RTX 50 GPUs to include older RTX 40-series cards. This confirmation follows modders successfully porting a leaked version of DLSS 5 to various hardware. The initial launch focus remains on RTX 50, with official RTX 40 support expected later this fall.

Despite modders enabling full control over DLSS 5 settings, Nvidia confirms that for gamers, it will remain a simple on-or-off toggle. Granular artistic controls, including model selection and intensity adjustments, are reserved for developers. However, the company noted that developers could potentially pass some controls through their own in-game settings menus.

A key benefit of DLSS 5 is its ease of integration, as its AI models automatically recognize and isolate objects in a scene. This allows for targeted neural lighting adjustments to specific elements like faces, foliage, or water droplets. Unreal Engine 5 already features a native plugin, and Nvidia also provides SDKs for integration.

DLSS 5 models run on every single frame, ensuring functionality without a minimum framerate requirement. Developers can apply the technology to entire games or specific scenes and cutscenes as needed. Nvidia is currently vague about previously announced titles, stating that "More games are on the way" and partners are finalizing integrations.

headline: Wikipedia Workers Unionize for the first time at Wikimedia Foundation
summary: Over 200 staffers at the Wikimedia Foundation, the nonprofit behind Wikipedia, have voted 158-14 to join the Communications Workers of America, marking a historic first.
details: More than 200 staffers at the Wikimedia Foundation, the nonprofit behind Wikipedia, have voted 158-14 to join the Communications Workers of America labor union. The US National Labor Relations Board counted ballots on Thursday, marking a historic first for the organization.

Employees state the union provides a mechanism to challenge management as Wikimedia faces growing competition from AI chatbots and a decline in volunteer editors. The foundation employs nearly 700 people globally, with the unionized contingent including software engineers, finance, and communications staff.

A lead technical program manager cited fear of retaliation among colleagues as a key motivator, aiming for more open debate across the organizational chart. This, she believes, is crucial for quick problem-solving and collective solutions.

The Wikimedia Foundation responded in a blog post, stating it will "approach this next phase constructively, lawfully, and with care for the staff." CEO Bernadette Meehan also expressed optimism in an internal email, acknowledging staff concerns.

The union drive was not primarily motivated by pay or benefits. Instead, frustrations over how the organization handled several hiring and firing decisions in the past year provided the final push needed for the vote.

Specific concerns included the disbanding of a team responsible for developing tools for volunteer editors and the removal of France from approved hiring locations for product and technology roles. These decisions highlighted a perceived lack of transparency and consultation.

In a show of solidarity, some volunteer Wikipedia editors organized a campaign this month to improve entries related to labor unions and related topics on the platform. This reflects broader sentiment for change.

Discussions about unionizing have occurred for a decade, but this is the first time an election was held. Momentum grew after a significant workforce expansion during the Covid pandemic introduced bureaucracy, leaving some employees feeling disempowered.

Despite a strong financial position with an annual budget over $200 million, Wikimedia faces challenges from AI companies scraping Wikipedia for training data, increasing server costs. Human traffic to Wikipedia is also declining as chatbots become a primary information source.

Staff worry these trends could diminish interest in contributing to Wikipedia, impacting content quality. They advocate for a bold push to make Wikipedia more attractive than AI, emphasizing that shaping this strategy requires input beyond management alone.
